Why is a cherry the topping of choice for milkshakes and not some other fruit?

I'm guessing here, but I'll give it a go.

Milkshakes became popular and widely available between the 1930's through 1950's, spurred by the invention of the electric blender and phase change refrigerators. Our food supply chain at that time was very different than it is now. Both transportation and refrigeration of the time hadn't reached the point where we could reliably get fresh fruit year round (with the exception of those that kept well; apples for instance). We relied on methods of preservation instead of intercontinental shipping to get our food.

Canning was the most the cheapest and most readily available means to keep fruit beyond the local season. This doesn't fully explain why cherries though. I suspect that was simply trial and error until people discovered that the super-sweet marichino cherry paired well with ice cream. Keep in mind that folks in the 1930s and 40s weren't living off the same sugar ridden, decadent diet that we do in N. America today. A milkshake was a treat not a staple and the super sweetness of a marichino cherry was a small decadence in itself.

Like I said though, just a guess. Anyone want to tell me how wrong I got it?
